utterances.text: No, that's not correct. The impression was that the uprising, the human resources, the manpower were getting organised and gradually taking the shape of a National Liberation Army. Gradually, we started to work on the formations and other military-related issues, so that we gave our best contribution to avoid ethnic war and just exercise pressure on the government, in order to achieve our goals, and we already discussed these issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The content of the communiques issued by the -- your organisation, the NLA, were then correct.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean by "correct" or "accurate"?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were they -- was the content of your communiques accurate?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The content of communique number 6 is accurate. These are demands. The same demands are enumerated in the memorandum, and they prevail to the very end of the war, which ended with the signing of the Ohrid Agreement and which also includes the same demands.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did the content of other communiques -- was the content of other communiques accurate?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not understand correctly the meaning of the word "accurate" that are you using. So could you please refer to another term, so that I'm clear on this. Could you please help me on this, so that I can provide with you an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was the content of the text issued by the -- by your organisation, NLA, truthful. Were they truthful?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the information and knowledge that we had at the time, and as we are talking now of the events that occurred six years ago, we did our best. The content of the communique truly expressed the standpoints of the NLA, its position that it opts for negotiations and not for use of force, and that it demands equality between ethnic Albanians and Albanians and other ethnic groups in the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did your communiques related to the actions carried out contain the truth. Were they truthful?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already answered your question, if it was correctly interpreted. Our aim, at the time, was that our communiques were accurate, were well understood, were true, based on the information and the knowledge that we possessed at the time when those communiques were drafted.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Therefore --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown P505 received in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is a communique signed by the General Staff, and in relation to the fighting on the 4th of May between the Macedonian state forces and the 113th Brigade. It contains the following, among others: "Military helicopters; M-26 -- my apologies, 24; 155-millimetre Howitzers; 120-millimetres cannons and various types of mortars; Katjushas tanks and armoured vehicles of the military and the police forces; struck, set ablaze, and destroyed the houses of Albanians. "The positions of the battalions in the village of Slupcane, Vaksince, violent fighting was waged with great heroism. The fighters of the 113th Kumanovo Brigade, Izmet Jashari, has so far killed 20 Macedonian soldiers. Police and militaries have taken three prisoners; one senior officer and two members of the paramilitary forces. "They have brought down two helicopters; one Mi-24, the other a military helicopter of another type. They have destroyed three tanks and four armoured vehicles, and they have taken a considerable amount of weapons." Is it correct that the NLA has taken down two helicopters of the Macedonian security forces, Mi-24.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This communique was drafted based on the information received from the brigade at the time. This is what the brigade thought; and for them and for us at that time, this information was accurate. As to its accuracy, the reports of the ARM should be consulted because they have the records of their own weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: According to you, is this communique truthful?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To me, it is accurate. For that, time this was true. I trusted my brigade and brigade trusted its own combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Macedonian version page 9, also English version page 9, this is the statement of the witness. Statement of the witness, P4987 [as interpreted]; paragraph 43, page 9 of both English and the Macedonian version. Can we please see page 9, and can we also pull up the Albanian version. It's paragraph 44. It would be page 12. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see the statement in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please enlarge paragraph 44 in the Albanian version so that the witness can read it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be really nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In your statement, paragraph 44, you say: "The brigades also bought military uniforms and weapons for themselves from various sources. Some units bought Strela 2M, AA portable missiles and used them against the ARM and police helicopter and winged aircraft. However, we could not shoot down any of them." In your statement, you say that you did not shoot done any helicopter. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This statement was written afterwards, during wartime. We had problems with the Mi-24 helicopters that the Republic of Macedonia purchased from Ukraine. These are armoured helicopters, and you cannot act against them, either with Strela 2M or anti-aircraft machine-guns. We could not act with Strela 2M because they have this equipment that emits heat; and if the rocket hits the helicopter, it would hit the body that is released from the helicopter. So maybe there were such targets and maybe soldiers thought that they have brought down a helicopter, but, in fact, they have shot at the defence system of these helicopters. But these were information during the development, during the war itself. My statement was given after the war, and it concerns impressions that I gained after the war was ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So the communique which I read before you earlier, accepted in evidence as P505, is not truthful?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are truths in it. There were casualties, losses suffered in manpower and equipment, but we took this information as true at the time we issued this communique.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the fighting in Macedonia, between the Macedonian security forces and the NLA, began already in January 2001?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have information from February. And if you have informations - and you should have such information because you were there, I was not; I was outside Macedonia - if you have information that the war started in January, then I would have no comments on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me when is the first of the operation or action carried out by your organisation, the NLA?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My information is that the uprising commenced at Tanuse; that, gradually, the brigade was starting to be formed; that it went out to the villages of Kumanovo and Lipkovo municipalities; then the development of the 112th brigade; and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So if any person claims before this Chamber that the first operation or action carried out the NLA organisation was on the 22nd of January in 2001, with the attack of the police station in Tearce near Tetovo, this would not be correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't in -- I wasn't in the Republic of Macedonia at the time, and I wasn't across the developments. I had my own problems where I was, and I was involved with a very important position and I wanted to -- to forget about everything else. So when I got back, I received information from the press, from the people, from friends that in Macedonia things -- things were happening the way they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you ask your commander, Ali Ahmeti, about that fact, when was the first NLA operation carried out?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't ask him. You're talking about operations. For me, operations mean large-scale participation of soldiers in an operation. If there was a -- such operation taking place, I should have known. But I haven't asked him about what happened before I went there, because the carrying out of my tasks were not related to what happened before. I remember that on the 16th, the killing of that child in Tanuse happened, the cause was not known; and then the uprising started, an uprising which I joined.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: On the 16th of which month?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: February, February. On the 16th of February.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. You stated that, at the level of brigades, there were solemn ceremonies taking place for the new recruits. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The brigades, on the basis of the rules, organised oath-taking ceremonies to instruct the recruits on the tasks they would have to undertake.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And all NLA members needed to give a ceremonial oath. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was part of the rules. It wasn't a law for the NLA. It was part of the rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And, in other words, there was no law governing the NLA --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: No law on NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The name of each of the new recruits was entered into the log that was kept at the level of brigade. You stated this at the page 7617 of the transcript, line 92, and the General Staff was informed about that. The brigade commanders informed the General Staff about that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. The volunteers were registered, they were assigned their duties, and when it came to the total numbers, they reported to the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The brigades also had other records, lists of weapons, guard shifts, daily log. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brigades had records that they kept; and on the basis of the rules that we sent over to them, they had to reconsider and they kept their own records. They had the lists of persons, how they were distributed among the units, and the weapons they carried, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And all those records were kept, and they remained in the brigades. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The brigades kept the records.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And the records remained with the brigades. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. They remained with the brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know Nazim Bushi?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him. I'm sorry that I replied instinctively.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: He was the commander of 114th Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi was a witness before this Tribunal, and was asked by my learned colleague Mettraux, on page 5870 of the transcript, line 17 to 24: "Do you remember, Mr. Bushi, being shown several documents, lists of documents? There was the model rules that shows membership in two separate brigades. Do you remember those documents being shown to you?" Mr. Bushi answered: "Yes, I recall that." After that, my colleague, Mr. Mettraux, asked him: "You indicate that you kept similar types of documents for your brigade. Do you recall that?" Mr. Bushi replied: "Yes." Then my colleague asked him: "Were you able to provide copies of those document to the Office of the Prosecutor?" That is page 5871 of the transcript, lines 1 to 4. Mr. Bushi said: "No. I surrendered the records of my brigade to the General Staff of the NLA at that time." Further on, my colleague asked him: "Do you know where those records are now?" The witness replied to this: "Gzim Ostreni would be able to tell you this." So is this the opposite of what you just testified about, that the documents remained with the brigades?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's accurate, that the documents remained with the brigades. Only the 116 Brigade sent material to me. I must stress that the source material, which were part of the General Staff archives, they were there and they remained there, because only the source documents, source material are of historic importance; whereas, the rest of the documents, which did not carry such importance, were -- remained with the brigades. The war stopped in 2001, and I haven't discussed about these issues with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does the NLA have an archive now?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Almost all the documents are here at The Hague. These are copies. I'm sure that there are documents, but it's the documents which you have had an opportunity to see. It's rules of service, the communiques, the instructions. A large number of the documents are here. I haven't given out copies of the documents that the -- that the government of the Republic of Macedonia had entered with other countries, such as Bulgaria, to buy weapons. I only gave them information that they needed, then I had information about tanks, models bought, models from 1972, from the same source as that of the Mi-24 helicopters. But I didn't find it proper to discuss other countries in this situation. I deemed that it was that was necessary to discuss internal issues within Macedonia in order to set records straight.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: For the duration of the conflict, in your opinion, the NLA troops were up to 5.000 members strong, including the operational, logistics department, various representatives, et cetera. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, around 5.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know how many members had the 114th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, it should have had more than 800.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know how many members had the 115th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around 750. It's quite a bit of time since it -- it happened, but I'll try and recall the figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But you don't have records to corroborate those figures. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've given to NATO the positions, and the signs have been placed on the map. On the 113th Brigade, it's the sign that there is more than two battalions. And on the basis of the flags and signs on the map, you-- we -- we show approximately the size of the brigade. The brigades of up to 600 members, there was one battalion; but if it was more than that, then there were two battalions. Such signs you can find only two on the map at 112 Brigade and 113 Brigade, but maybe we should refer to the document itself to be most accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please tell me -- very well. I will go back to the NLA members issue when we will be reviewing the maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, would this be the convenient time for the break or is it too early? I apologise. I apologise. With regards to the number of NLA members, could the witness please be shown the statement of the commander, Ali Ahmeti, 65 ter 2D325, paragraph 35, page 7 in both the Macedonian and the English versions. Could the paragraph 35 in the Macedonian version be zoomed in on, so that the witness could see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: "The NLA had around 6.000 uniformed soldiers," and then it continues with other issues. So could you agree with me that the assessment that there is a discrepancy in the assessment of the NLA members between you and your commander and that it amounts to around 20 per cent?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right, because here I haven't included the medical staff, who only in the 112 consisted of 500 people, doctors and so on, because we had to cover a vast wave of territory where there were no doctors or nurses. I think that this is what constitutes the difference in figures, as compared to Mr. Ali Ahmeti said.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does the medical battalion belong to the logistics section?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it had operated independently. We could say it was at the level of battalion, and it was looking after the health. It was looking after the wounded, and after the people who needed treatment. It was directly reporting to the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But, at any rate, it belongs to the logistics.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's normal that it should be part of logistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could I refresh your memory by showing you your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit P497, paragraph 21, page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In paragraph 21, you say: "For the duration of the armed conflict in Macedonia, I would estimate that the strength of the NLA reached the figure of 5.000 at its highest. This figure includes the operational part, the logistic part, the different representatives, and others." Is it correct that when you were giving your statement to the investigators of the ICTY Office of the Prosecutor, you spoke about the total number of 5.000?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was speaking about the total number for the people who were in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And this comprises the logistics as well?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The part of the logistics that were uniformed, but there were some ambulances which served outside our formations. Of course, they were under the auspices of the brigade, and they were looking after the health of the brigades. This was an army of volunteers. The number wasn't the same each day, but this was -- this was an approximation. And, at the end, I was saying there were 5.000 uniformed members.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So how many NLA members were there who were not wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were carrying uniforms, but not all were carrying weapons because we did not have enough weapons. So there was a selection, especially those who had support weapons, like mortars anti-aircraft weapons. They were entitled to a personal weapon. There the number of weapons was reduced, and this was a unit which was deep inside the formation of a brigade. So an 82-millimetre mortar should have about five, six soldiers, and all the soldiers had the same mortar and they should also carry personal weapons. But in the circumstances, not all of them had personal weapons because we didn't have them. The cooks didn't have a weapon. So there was -- the weapons were distributed selectively, trying to give weapons to all those who were essentially for the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you tell my colleague Mettraux before this Tribunal about undercover NLA members at Kicevo, Debar, and Struga? Does this figure include those members as well?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The figure includes all those members who were in the position of the -- positions of the brigade and who were actively serving the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yesterday, on page 7631 of the transcript, you stated that the commander of the 116 Brigade, Tahir Sinani, was killed, together with four other people, while trying to create an explosive device. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recall where was he killed?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was killed in Kuku Zabel, in the vicinity of Tanuse, or another village, in the municipality of Mavrovo [as interpreted] now.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I apologise. Was it interpreted well? In the municipality Tanusevci, near Mavrovo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It wasn't correctly translated. It is on the mountainous area, the place is called Kuku Zabel, in the vicinity of Tanuse, a village which is in the -- the municipality of Gostivar, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. This is a bit more precise information. Were the persons who were killed together with him, those four persons, were they NLA members?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me when were they killed?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 29th of June, I think. I have to remember many dates. But if I'm mistaken, I apologise for that. I think it was on the 29th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: At any rate, it was in the month of June, during the military conflict?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, would now be the convenient time for the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness Ostreni, in your statement, you stay that during the conflict, NLA lost a total of 68 people, including civilians of Albanian ethnic origin. Do you recall saying this?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The persons who died in Ljuboten in 2001, are they included in this number of 68 persons?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This I don't know. I provided the OTP with this number based on the information I had in the NLA and that I obtained later from the families of the martyrs. So I don't know whether this number includes those persons who died there.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So when you said in your statement that, during the conflict the NLA lost a total of 68 persons including civilians of Albanian ethnic original, this number is not verified and correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave a figure that I knew. In order to verify its accuracy, I need to go through the lists and see each member one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: To the Prosecution, in giving your statement, you gave a list of deceased members of the NLA. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall this.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown R062-6984 [as interpreted], 65 ter 212. Can the witness be assisted. There's also a hard copy version of this list. Perhaps, he can be given this one as well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know this list?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. According to what I see, it's a list containing 52 persons. It looks like a list provided by me, but it is not completed fully. A long time has gone, so that's why I'm saying that maybe I provided this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you sure that you provided this list to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not certain, because I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness -- to refresh the witness's memory, can the witness please be shown P497, the statement of Mr. Ostreni, page 12 in the English and Macedonian version. In the Albanian version, there are two pages. Can you please scroll down two pages in the Albanian version. One page further down in the Albanian version, please. One page further down, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, do you see under number 15 of the document which you provided to the Prosecution -- Office of the Prosecution, and that it states: "List of fallen NLA members."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can item number 15 please be enlarged so that the witness can see it better.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you repeat the number again, please. Now I see it, and now I'm certain that I provided the list. There was a large number of documents, and it was impossible for me to remember each and every one of them. So I apologise for not recalling.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is a list of fallen NLA members. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we open, once again, R062-6984. It's 65 ter 212.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: According to you, is this a list of fallen members of the NLA during the crisis of 2001?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I have in the Albanian language or the one in English on the screen? Which one?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The one you see in hard copy in the Albanian language, which is in front of you.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This should be the record, the list that we drafted; and in association with the War Veteran Association, this list needed to be verified and checked whether all those persons are mentioned there.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is this list accurate?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I cannot say, because we don't have the date when it was drafted. Maybe there is someone who is left out from the list, so maybe it's not fully accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You do not know the date when this list was prepared?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It contains the dates when those members were killed, and I think that the list was drafted in late August. So this is the time when this list should have been drafted.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The first page contains the logo of the National Liberation Army, and it should be a document -- no, an official document of the National Liberation Army?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a record, a document that, in fact, shows a record kept about the fallen members of the NLA at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see on the document that there is a place and date when a person had fallen. Do you see this? This is in column 5 and 6. Do you see this in front of you?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see the name of Tahir Sinani on this list?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't see his name, but that's why I said in the very beginning that this list is not completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The other persons together -- that, together with Tahir Sinani, fell are not in this list. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember their names. But if they're not there, they're not there. That's why I pointed out that fact that this list is not full. It's not complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But as a place of falling, Tanuse is not -- in the area of Gostivar, is not listed anywhere?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the name Tahir Sinani is not there for the location where he fell to be mentioned. Had his name been mentioned, then the place where he fell would have been mentioned, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When Tahir Sinani fell, was your chief -- was your General Staff informed of this in June and July in 2001?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was informed on the same day by Tallat Xhaferi, who was at that time with that brigade. Afterwards, I issued a communique in order to inform the public opinion and his family; and in this communique, I expressed my condolences for his death and the death of his friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Although you said that this document -- you were informed of this document in August, the person who prepared this document still did not have this information about his -- him having lost his life. Would you agree with this?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with that. I already stated that we issued a communique to the media, to the press; and all those who followed the events and who heard about that were aware of what happened, of that incident. I personally, with my comrades, visited the house where his brothers were residing to express my condolences. So the falling of Mr. Tahir Sinani and his comrades was not something I that was not aware of. I would say that this was a mistake because his name and the names of the -- his comrades that fell, together with him, should be on this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When you gave the statement on the 27th and 29th of July, 2005 to the Prosecution, you -- you informed them of this discrepancy in this list?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that, whether I informed them of this or whether we discussed this issue. I just remember that, among other documents, I handed them over this document, so that they had as much information as possible regarding the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell this Chamber the total number of NLA members that have fallen during the conflict of 2001?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that, maybe not that accurate, in my head the information that I had was 68, together with the number of the civilians; while the number of the uniformed persons - and, again, I would mention here that this is a personal assessment; I'm not that accurate - but my belief is that it's about 38 to 40 persons who were in uniform out of this figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did your commander, Ali Ahmeti, have information about how many members of the NLA fell during the conflict in 2001?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. Maybe he had such information, but he should say that. Even myself, if I go to -- back to these documents and consult with the War Veteran Association, I would have come with the accurate figure. But now, here, I'm under oath and I'm talking of things that I know. And regarding this issue, I give you my assessment about the figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were there persons from Kosovo members of the NLA that fell in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were, yes, and there are such in the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were there persons from Albania as well?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe there were. I know for one, for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell who this person is?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is martyr. He is a fallen soldier. His name is Kurlat. It is quite difficult to pronounce. I don't know his last name, but he fell during the combat activities of 112th Brigade. I believe that there were others as well, but I don't remember their names right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown the statement of Ali Ahmeti; 65 ter 2D-325, page 10 in the English version, 9 in the Macedonian version, item 56.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In item 56, which pertains to casualties, your commander Ali Ahmeti says: "Throughout the whole armed conflict in Macedonia, the NLA had 65 members killed. I do not know the exact number of wounded. Civilian casualties from among the Albanian community were about 50 men and women, including about ten children mostly killed by artillery shelling." Could you concur with me that your assessment and the assessment of your commander differ, in double.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that these are different assessments. This is a figure that I had in my head. Really, the best solution would be to go back to the exact records. As I pointed out, this was an issue that the War Veteran Association dealt with later on. They are the accurate information, who fell, when they fell, when they were wounded, in which location, and where they were treated. A law is being prepared in the Republic of Macedonia that would include these persons or their families. So I agree with you, there is a difference between what my assessment is and what his assessment is.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When giving the statement to the Prosecutor, this remark -- you did not give this remark to him. You did not say that this was not an accurate figure, which is approximately close to that number.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will stress, again, that in my memory, and based on my knowledge, there were 68 persons killed. He gave a figure of 65. The list contains 52. So I apologise that we are talking in these terms about fallen soldiers, about martyrs, but it is easily to check and verify these numbers because there are records for all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown Exhibit 515. This is -- these are maps. Can the court usher please give the witness a hard copy of this document, so we can have a closer look at them. Can we please open the first page, and can we please see 515, P515-1 -- /1. This is the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You stated that this map was marked by you.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: It depicts the territory under the NLA control in 2001.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking about Brigade 112 and 115.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes. That was going to be my next question. Is it correct that those were the areas under the control of 112th and 115th Brigade. Since you stated that you could tell me about the numbers of troops in the brigades, once we opened the maps, could you now tell me what was the number of troops in the 112th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 112th Brigade, according to the information that I had at the time, had about 1.200 members.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And could you tell me about the 115th Brigade. What was the number of members there?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 115th Brigade, at the time, should have had more than 750 members.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Considering that the left-hand side of the map is unmarked, could you explain whether this is the border of the territory under the NLA control in 2001?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the left-hand side, we're talking about north, south, east, and west. We are talking about borders of which installation? If you can help me, which side of the map are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is to the north-west of Tetovo. At the end, the map ends in white space, to put it in simple terms; and then it is adjacent to the border of the Republic of Macedonia, where there is a blue line marking it. The border of the Republic of Macedonia and the blue line on the left side of the map are not joined. Was this the border of the area under the NLA control, where the map ends, on the left side?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the information that I had from the brigades, it's from Bogovinje on the right, on the left-hand border of the brigade to the west of Vratnica, without including Odri.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that in the area marked on the map, the one that you state was under the NLA control, there is no city?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are villages, as we know. The cease-fire reached -- was reached when the situation was like this, and it was reached an agreement with the NATO so that we could withdraw from the villages, so that we could not hinder the free movement of the villagers, of the people there. There was no city which the 112th Brigade controlled?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Do you see the village of Pirok?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher help the witness mark the village with the number 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please help me to find the village of Pirok first.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: It is in the lower part of the map. It would be to the south-west.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you mark it in the e-court on the screen before you?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: One moment. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And please write number 1 next to it.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's -- it's very small, the writing. I'm not sure whether I've marked it correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, you've marked it correctly. Is it correct that Pirok was not under the NLA control?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the information that I had when I drafted this map, it should have been like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could this also be valid about the situation at the end of the conflict, I would say, the 13th of August?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have tried, including the monitors, that this line be kept, because at the same time, when the General Staff of the NLA gave this document to NATO, the army of Yugoslavia -- of Macedonia gave its own maps to NATO on the position -- positions. I believe that -- that we tried to maintain the situation as we've declared it, but this is a map 1:200.000, and a thick line that I have drawn covers 200 metres or so. But, mainly, this is the line that we tried to keep with the NLA and not to move from this line.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: There is a highway between Tetovo and Gostivar. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: There is also the old road going from Tetovo to Gostivar.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about the road on the left or on the right of the highway? Are we talking about the road on the left?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: On the left side, going through Pirok.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tetovo-Gostivar or Gostivar-Tetovo?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: From Tetovo to Gostivar, since we see Tetovo here on the map.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you go from Tetovo to Gostivar, Pirok is on the right-hand side, not on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But it goes -- that road goes through Pirok.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The highway does not go through --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm asking but the old road?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm asking for your help, so that can I reply correctly, and I have no other tendency. The highway from Tetovo to Gostivar, on its right-hand side, it's the old road, which goes through Pirok.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes. And according to the map, the old road, Tetovo-Gostivar, was not under the NLA control in 2001.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We agreed that this line of the positions not to be marked on the road, so that the citizens could go on with their everyday activities. So that's why this line follows the line of the road, but these couple of millimetres on the map are, in fact, an area enough for the citizens to go on with their everyday activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So the road was not under the NLA control.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This map shows that the line is parallel to the line depicting the old road. So if you consider the fact that a soldier has a weapon with him and that the fire range, the average is 400 metres, then I don't know what to say as to your question whether the road is under the NLA control or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Do you see in the upper part the village of Vratnica, in the upper part of the map? It is slightly to the east.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see Vratnica, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please mark it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be helped.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will do my best to mark it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Please mark it with the number 2.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And Vratnica was not under the NLA control as well. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The map speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. You can also see in front of you the road Tetovo-Skopje.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the highway?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it, but it's up to Bukovic on the map, not up to Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And in the section you see in front of you, to the south from the road, Tetovo to Skopje, the territory was not under the NLA control, or at least it is not marked as being under the NLA control?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. It is not marked here because the information I got from the brigade spoke to the effect how I represent it on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could I seek to tender this map into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D82, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps this would be the convenient time for the break, and I will try to finish my cross-examination of this witness within the first of tomorrow's sessions, just for the information of the Chamber and the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. The Chamber would mention that it understands the next witness would normally expect or feel it would be desirable to have German interpretation. We would be concerned that we may well lose even a full day because German interpretation cannot be arranged until Friday. Do you think, Mr. Saxon, that the witness might be able at least to have his evidence in chief heard using English, in which he has some facility?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The Prosecution believes that would be possible and, therefore, the Prosecution believes the next witness could commence his direct examination beginning on Thursday morning. If I may, just respectfully, provide a small caveat. There is an outstanding motion, I believe it's called the 7th motion, to add -- for permission to add some exhibits to the Prosecution's list of exhibits. It would certainly be helpful if that -- if a decision could be given on that motion prior to the start of the next witness's evidence. Because depending on that decision, that would affect certain aspects of direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And how long would you anticipate for direct examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Approximately one full court day, possibly a bit longer, but we are trying to keep it within one full court day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. Well, thank you for that, Mr. Saxon, and I think we will endeavour do hear the evidence in chief of the witness without German interpretation on Thursday, in the hope that we can avoid losing a full day that way. There are a small number of decisions that are in the process of completion at the present time, and I believe the one you mentioned is among them. We will adjourn now and resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
